destination_record.name: Sikkim
destination_record.tagline: Himalayan monasteries, high lakes and Kanchenjunga views, from Gangtok to Tsomgo Lake, Yumthang Valley and Pelling.
destination_record.places: Gangtok, Tsomgo (Changu) Lake, Nathu La, Lachung, Yumthang Valley, Ravangla, Pelling, Darjeeling (optional add-on)

on.places: Gangtok, Tsomgo Lake, Pelling, Ravangla, Lachung and Yumthang Valley
on.activities: Clear mountain views, sightseeing at monasteries and viewpoints, and flower-filled valleys in spring. These months suit most trips, including Lachung and Yumthang.

off.activities: Heavy rain, green hills and lower prices. Landslides can delay roads, especially towards North Sikkim, and views are often hidden by cloud, so plans may change at short notice.

mid.places: Gangtok, Pelling, Tsomgo Lake and Yumthang Valley
mid.activities: Cold, clear days with snow at Tsomgo Lake, Lachung and Yumthang, and good Kanchenjunga views. High roads can close after snow, so we plan flexibly.

profile.overview:
Sikkim is a small Himalayan state between Nepal, Bhutan and Tibet, with Kanchenjunga, the world's third-highest peak, filling the western skyline. In a few days you can go from the monasteries and cafes of Gangtok to the high waters of Tsomgo Lake, the meadows of Yumthang Valley and the quiet ridge-top town of Pelling.

It is clean, safe and easy to travel, and a favourite with Indian families, couples and friends who want mountain scenery without a long trek. Roads are winding, so days are shorter than the map suggests. Tell us your dates, group size and comfort level, and we will build the route around you, with permits arranged.

facts.languages: Nepali, Sikkimese (Bhutia), Lepcha, Hindi and English
facts.climate: Mild in Gangtok, cold and snowy at altitude from December to February, heavy rain from June to September
facts.flight_time: Delhi to Bagdogra is about 2 hr 15 min by air; Chennai usually has a one-stop flight; trains run to New Jalpaiguri; then 4 to 5 hr by road

reasons.title: Mountains close at hand
reasons.text: Kanchenjunga views, high lakes and alpine valleys are all within a few hours' drive of each other.

reasons.title: Monasteries and living culture
reasons.text: Rumtek, Pemayangtse and Enchey show Buddhist traditions that are part of everyday life in Sikkim.

reasons.title: Clean, calm and easy
reasons.text: Sikkim is known for tidy towns, polite drivers and a relaxed pace, which suits families and senior parents.

reasons.title: Snow and flowers
reasons.text: Winter brings snow to Tsomgo Lake and Yumthang, and spring brings rhododendrons and clear skies.

reasons.title: Easy to reach
reasons.text: Fly to Bagdogra or take a train to New Jalpaiguri, then drive into the hills.

attractions.title: Tsomgo (Changu) Lake
attractions.text: A glacial lake at about 3,780 m, ringed by mountains and often frozen in winter.

attractions.title: Nathu La
attractions.text: A high mountain pass on the Sikkim border at about 4,310 m, open to Indian citizens with a permit, on certain days and in good weather.

attractions.title: Yumthang Valley
attractions.text: A high valley north of Lachung with meadows, a river and hot springs, known for spring flowers and winter snow.

attractions.title: Lachung
attractions.text: A mountain village in North Sikkim and the usual base for Yumthang.

attractions.title: Gangtok and MG Marg
attractions.text: The capital's pedestrian promenade, with cafes, shops and views of the hills.

attractions.title: Rumtek Monastery
attractions.text: A large monastery near Gangtok and an important seat of the Karma Kagyu school.

attractions.title: Pemayangtse Monastery and Rabdentse
attractions.text: A historic monastery near Pelling and the ruins of Sikkim's old capital.

attractions.title: Buddha Park, Ravangla
attractions.text: A large seated Buddha statue set among hills near the town of Ravangla.

experiences.title: Kanchenjunga sunrise
experiences.text: Watch the first light on the range from Pelling or a Gangtok viewpoint, in clear weather.

experiences.title: Gangtok ropeway
experiences.text: A short cable-car ride that gives a wide view over the city and the valley.

experiences.title: Yak ride at Tsomgo Lake
experiences.text: An optional short ride by the lake, popular with families, paid locally.

experiences.title: Snow in Lachung and Yumthang
experiences.text: From December to February the high valleys are white, with cold, clear days.

experiences.title: Monastery visit
experiences.text: Join the quiet of a morning at a monastery, with prayer flags, butter lamps and mountain air.

experiences.title: River rafting on the Teesta
experiences.text: A seasonal and optional rafting stretch, usually in the drier months and subject to water levels.

food.title: Momos and thukpa
food.text: Steamed dumplings and noodle soup, the everyday comfort food of Sikkim.

food.title: Sikkimese thali
food.text: Rice, dal and local greens, sometimes with gundruk, a tangy fermented-leaf dish.

food.title: Sel roti and local tea
food.text: A ring-shaped rice bread served at festivals and breakfasts, with hot tea from nearby gardens.

food.title: Temi tea
food.text: Tea from the Temi garden near Ravangla, one of the best-known in the state.

food.title: Vegetarian and Jain meals
food.text: Vegetarian momos and dal-rice are easy to find, and we can arrange Indian vegetarian and Jain meal options.

tips.title: Carry photo ID for everyone
tips.text: Aadhaar, passport, voter ID or a driving licence is needed for hotels and permits.

tips.title: Take it slowly at altitude
tips.text: Tsomgo Lake, Nathu La, Lachung and Yumthang are high. Drink water, rest and avoid rushing.

tips.title: Pack warm layers
tips.text: Even in summer, nights are cool in the hills and cold at altitude. Thermals and a windproof jacket help.

tips.title: Plan for slow roads
tips.text: Distances look short, but winding roads mean most transfers take 3 to 7 hours.

tips.title: Keep cash handy
tips.text: ATMs and mobile networks can be patchy outside Gangtok, especially in Lachung and Yumthang.

tips.title: Respect monasteries
tips.text: Dress modestly, remove shoes where asked and ask before photographing inside.

travel_info.visa: Indian citizens need no visa to travel in Sikkim, but every traveller must carry a valid photo ID such as an Aadhaar card, passport, voter ID or driving licence. Some places, including Tsomgo Lake, Nathu La and parts of North Sikkim, need permits, and Nathu La is open only on certain days and to Indian citizens. We arrange permits and confirm the current rules at booking.
travel_info.health: No compulsory vaccinations from India. Altitude sickness can affect some travellers at Tsomgo Lake, Nathu La, Lachung and Yumthang, so go slowly, drink water and seek medical advice beforehand if you have heart, breathing or blood pressure problems. Carry personal medicines and motion-sickness tablets for winding roads.
travel_info.money: Carry some cash, as ATMs and mobile networks can be patchy outside Gangtok, especially in Lachung and Yumthang. UPI and cards work in many hotels and shops in Gangtok and Pelling. Tipping drivers and guides is customary but optional.

faqs.q: How many days do I need for Sikkim?
faqs.a: Five to six nights covers Gangtok, Tsomgo Lake and Pelling. Seven nights lets you add Lachung and Yumthang at an easier pace.

faqs.q: Do I need permits for Sikkim?
faqs.a: Indian citizens need no visa, but some places, such as Tsomgo Lake, Nathu La and parts of North Sikkim, need permits. We arrange permits and confirm the current rules at booking.
No. Nathu La is open to Indian citizens on certain days of the week and in good weather, with a permit, so it cannot be guaranteed. If it is closed, we add another local sight.

faqs.q: When is the best time to go?
faqs.a: March to May and October to November have clearer skies and good views. December to February is cold with snow at altitude, and June to September is the rainy season with a risk of landslides.
Most travellers fly to Bagdogra (IXB) or take a train to New Jalpaiguri, then drive. Pakyong Airport near Gangtok also exists, but flights there are limited and vary.
Yes. Darjeeling is about 3 to 4 hours by road from Bagdogra and can be added as an optional extension. Ask us for a quote.

group_trips.title: Sikkim Gangtok, Lachung, Yumthang and Pelling Group Trip
group_trips.summary: Seven days across Sikkim with Gangtok, Tsomgo Lake, Nathu La where permitted, Lachung and Yumthang Valley, and the Kanchenjunga views of Pelling, with a trip captain.
group_trips.overview:
This fixed-departure group trip covers the best of Sikkim in six nights: two in Gangtok, one in Lachung, one more in Gangtok and two in Pelling. You visit Tsomgo Lake and, where permits and the day allow, Nathu La, then drive north to Lachung and the high meadows of Yumthang Valley.

You then return to Gangtok and travel west to Pelling, where Pemayangtse Monastery, the ruins of Rabdentse and the Chenrezig statue sit below the Kanchenjunga range. A trip captain travels with the group, and Indian meal options are available on request.

Roads are winding and the Lachung leg has long driving days, so the pace is planned with rest in mind. We arrange the permits and share altitude advice at booking.

Gangtok's MG Marg and Rumtek Monastery
Overnight stay in Lachung, in the mountains of North Sikkim
Yumthang Valley, with meadows, a river and hot springs

Chenrezig statue and Skywalk, with Kanchenjunga views in clear weather

itinerary.title: Arrival at Bagdogra | Drive to Gangtok
itinerary.description:
Arrive at Bagdogra Airport or New Jalpaiguri station and meet your trip captain.
Drive to Gangtok, about 4 to 5 hours by road, with a stop for lunch on the way.
Check in at your hotel and rest after the journey.
Stroll along MG Marg in the evening if you feel fresh.
Overnight stay in Gangtok.

itinerary.title: Tsomgo Lake | Baba Mandir | Nathu La (subject to permit)
itinerary.description:
After an early breakfast, drive up to Tsomgo (Changu) Lake, at about 3,780 m.
Continue to Baba Mandir and, where the permit and the day allow, on to Nathu La.
If Nathu La is closed, we add another sight near Gangtok instead.
Return to Gangtok by late afternoon and enjoy a free evening.
Overnight stay in Gangtok.

itinerary.title: Gangtok to Lachung | Waterfalls and River Valleys
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, check out and drive north towards Lachung, about 6 to 7 hours with stops.
Pause at roadside waterfalls and viewpoints, and have lunch on the way.
Check in at your Lachung stay and rest while you adjust to the altitude.
Dinner is served at the stay.
Overnight stay in Lachung.

itinerary.title: Yumthang Valley | Return to Gangtok
itinerary.description:
After an early breakfast, drive to Yumthang Valley, about 25 km from Lachung.
Walk among the meadows and river, and see the hot springs; the valley has flowers in spring and snow in winter.
Return to Lachung for lunch, then drive back to Gangtok, a long day on the road.
Arrive in Gangtok in the evening and check in.
Overnight stay in Gangtok.

itinerary.title: Gangtok to Pelling | Rumtek Monastery
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, check out and visit Rumtek Monastery near Gangtok.
Drive west to Pelling, about 5 to 6 hours in all, with a lunch stop.
Check in at your hotel and enjoy the mountain air.
Spend the evening at leisure.

itinerary.description:
After breakfast, visit Pemayangtse Monastery.

Visit the Chenrezig statue and Skywalk, for views of the Kanchenjunga range in clear weather.
Return to the hotel and enjoy a free evening.
Overnight stay in Pelling.

itinerary.description:
After breakfast, check out of the hotel.
Drive to Bagdogra Airport or New Jalpaiguri station, about 5 to 6 hours by road.
Book an afternoon or evening departure to allow for the road journey.

honeymoon_trips.title: Sikkim Honeymoon: Gangtok, Ravangla and Pelling with Kanchenjunga Views
honeymoon_trips.summary: Six unhurried nights for two across Gangtok, Ravangla and Pelling, with Tsomgo Lake, the Ravangla Buddha statue, a candlelight dinner, a couples spa session and a private Kanchenjunga sunrise drive.
honeymoon_trips.overview:
This private honeymoon moves slowly through the quieter side of Sikkim: two nights in Gangtok, two in Ravangla and two in Pelling. You travel by private car, start most mornings late and keep afternoons and evenings for each other.

Gangtok brings Tsomgo Lake, Rumtek Monastery and a ropeway ride over the city. Ravangla offers the great Buddha statue and cool mountain air, and Pelling ends the trip with a private sunrise drive to a Kanchenjunga viewpoint, weather permitting.

Expect a flower welcome on arrival, a candlelight dinner and a couples spa session, all subject to availability. Tell us your wedding date at booking and we will pass it to the hotels.

custom_trips.title: Sikkim Classic Circuit: Gangtok, Ravangla and Pelling
custom_trips.summary: A private six-night circuit through Gangtok, Ravangla and Pelling, with Tsomgo Lake, Nathu La where permitted, Rumtek, the Ravangla Buddha statue and Kanchenjunga views.
custom_trips.overview:
This private classic circuit follows the traditional route through Sikkim: three nights in Gangtok, one in Ravangla and two in Pelling. You see Tsomgo Lake and, where the permit and the day allow, Nathu La, then visit Rumtek Monastery and the Buddha statue at Ravangla.

Pelling completes the trip with Pemayangtse Monastery, the ruins of Rabdentse and views of the Kanchenjunga range. You travel by private AC vehicle, and the plan can be adjusted to your dates and pace.

After an early breakfast, drive up to Tsomgo (Changu) Lake, at about 3,780 m.
Continue to Baba Mandir and, where the permit and the day allow, on to Nathu La.
If Nathu La is closed, we add another sight near Gangtok instead.
Return to Gangtok by late afternoon.
Overnight stay in Gangtok.

itinerary.title: Gangtok Sightseeing | Rumtek Monastery
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, visit Rumtek Monastery near Gangtok.
Stop at Enchey Monastery, Ganesh Tok and Tashi View Point.
Spend the afternoon on MG Marg for shopping and cafes.
Overnight stay in Gangtok.

itinerary.title: Gangtok to Ravangla | Buddha Park
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, check out and drive to Ravangla, about 3 to 4 hours by road.
Visit Buddha Park and its large seated Buddha statue.
Check in at your hotel and enjoy the cool evening air.
Overnight stay in Ravangla.

itinerary.title: Ravangla to Pelling
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, check out and drive to Pelling, about 3 hours by road.
Check in at your hotel and relax.
Spend the evening at leisure with views of the hills.
Overnight stay in Pelling.

itinerary.title: Pemayangtse | Rabdentse | Chenrezig Statue and Skywalk
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, visit Pemayangtse Monastery.
Walk through the ruins of Rabdentse, the old capital of Sikkim.
Visit the Chenrezig statue and Skywalk, for views of the Kanchenjunga range in clear weather.
Overnight stay in Pelling.

itinerary.title: Departure from Bagdogra
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, check out of the hotel.
Drive to Bagdogra Airport or New Jalpaiguri station, about 5 to 6 hours by road.
Book an afternoon or evening departure to allow for the road journey.

custom_trips.title: Sikkim Family Holiday: Gangtok and Pelling at an Easy Pace
custom_trips.summary: A private six-night family holiday in Gangtok and Pelling, with the zoo, the ropeway, a Tsomgo Lake day, a Buddha statue stop at Ravangla and easy sightseeing around Pelling.
custom_trips.overview:
This family holiday keeps the driving manageable and the days varied: three nights in Gangtok and three in Pelling. In Gangtok you ride the ropeway, visit the Himalayan Zoological Park and take a day trip to Tsomgo Lake, which can be skipped or shortened for young children or senior parents.

On the way to Pelling you stop at the Buddha statue in Ravangla. Pelling has easy sightseeing, with Pemayangtse Monastery, the ruins of Rabdentse, Khecheopalri Lake and the Chenrezig statue. Tell us the ages in your group and we will adjust the plan.
highlights: Gangtok ropeway and the Himalayan Zoological Park
Tsomgo (Changu) Lake day trip, which can be shortened for children or seniors
Rumtek Monastery and Gangtok viewpoints
A stop at the Buddha statue in Ravangla on the road to Pelling
Pemayangtse Monastery and the ruins of Rabdentse
Khecheopalri Lake and the Chenrezig statue near Pelling
Private AC vehicle, with a relaxed pace

itinerary.description:
After breakfast, drive to Khecheopalri Lake, a sacred and peaceful lake set among forest.
Return to Pelling and spend the afternoon at leisure.
Overnight stay in Pelling.

custom_trips.title: North Sikkim Explorer: Tsomgo Lake, Lachung and Yumthang Valley
custom_trips.summary: A private five-night mountain trip for travellers who want high-altitude scenery, with Tsomgo Lake, Nathu La where permitted, two nights in Lachung and a full day at Yumthang Valley.
custom_trips.overview:
This private trip focuses on the high country of Sikkim. You base yourself in Gangtok for two nights, visit Tsomgo Lake and, where permits and the day allow, Nathu La, then drive north to Lachung for two nights.

A full day at Yumthang Valley, with the option to go on towards Zero Point where the road and permit allow, gives you time among the meadows, river and hot springs. It is a high, cold trip with long drives, best for travellers who are fit and comfortable at altitude.
highlights: Tsomgo (Changu) Lake, and Nathu La where permits and the day allow
Two nights in Lachung, in the mountains of North Sikkim
Full day at Yumthang Valley, with meadows, river and hot springs
Optional drive towards Zero Point where the road and permit allow
Snow in winter, and rhododendrons and flowers in spring
Permits arranged by us and private AC vehicle

Where the road and permit allow, continue towards Zero Point, at over 4,500 m; otherwise spend longer in the valley.
Return to Lachung for the evening.
Overnight stay in Lachung.
